changeSet.author: nexus-net63
changeSet.comment: Grant nexus_svc role the DML privileges it needs on the nexus and t1 schemas. REQUIRED: nexus_svc must exist before first migration; if missing, GRANT fails loudly and migration aborts (fail-fast — no silent skip). runAlways: re-executed on every startup so a role created after the first migration is automatically provisioned on the next restart. Owner-restricted per-relation iteration (nexus-46yy3 class, GH #1402, nexus-0gis0): the bulk GRANT ... ON ALL TABLES/SEQUENCES form hard-errors on any relation this role (nexus_admin, NOSUPERUSER) does not own — specifically the deliberately superuser-owned nexus.diag_chash_conformance view (RLS-exempt owner required, nexus-vounk) — aborting every engine boot once the view exists. Foreign-owned relations are intentionally skipped: nexus_svc does not need access to them, and only their owner can grant on them anyway.

changeSet.author: hal
changeSet.comment: nexus-pebfx.4: the /version endpoint reports the applied Liquibase journal (schema_latest_id, schema_changeset_count) for the nx-client/JAR version handshake. The journal tables are created by Liquibase under the migration (admin) role; the service role needs read access. runAlways for the same self-healing reason as grants-001.
changeSet.sql: GRANT SELECT ON public.databasechangelog TO nexus_svc; GRANT SELECT ON public.databasechangeloglock TO nexus_svc;

changeSet.author: nexus-0ys55
changeSet.comment:
nexus-0ys55: MAINTAIN on the five purge-trash VACUUM targets (nexus.chunks_384, nexus.chunks_768, nexus.chunks_1024, nexus.catalog_document_chunks, nexus.catalog_documents) -- mirrors the RETIRED chash_alias MAINTAIN grant that used to precede this one (grants-nexus-svc-1, rdr180-17/F2, removed at nexus-lgdel.l1) EXACTLY: same PG17+ version guard, same runAlways self-healing placement, same reason a GRANT is required at all -- nexus_svc holds DML only and does not own these tables (nexus_admin does), and PostgreSQL does NOT error when a non-owner without MAINTAIN vacuums a table -- it emits a WARNING (observed on a live PG17 instance: permission denied to vacuum "<table>", skipping it) and silently no-ops it. Without this grant, CatalogRepository#purgeTrash's post-commit VACUUM (ANALYZE) step (TenantScope#vacuumAnalyze), run asynchronously off the HTTP request thread (nexus-tyxnh), would never actually vacuum on a real production purge, defeating the bead's whole point (a live 11,594-document purge left ~60k dead tuples an operator had to VACUUM by hand) -- every sweep would warn- and-skip silently in the vacuum executor's own log, invisible to the synchronous HTTP response either way.
TABLE-LIST LOCKSTEP: this list, TenantScope.VACUUM_ALLOWED_TABLES, and CatalogRepository.PURGE_VACUUM_TABLES must all name the SAME five tables. Each of those three call sites carries a comment pointing at the other two, and TenantScopeVacuumMaintainGrantParityTest asserts the two Java lists agree -- update all three together or the allowlist / grant / sweep-target sets can silently drift. THIS CHANGESET'S OWN table list is pinned only BEHAVIORALLY, not by a static textual assertion against the Java lists (a changeset SQL string has no Java symbol to compare against): CatalogPurgeTrashVacuumTest's default-nexus_svc-role "real vacuum" proof (verified via pg_stat_user_tables.last_vacuum) is what actually catches this changeset's table list drifting out of lockstep with the other two -- if it silently stops covering all five, this pin is gone and nothing else replaces it.
MAINTAIN is PostgreSQL 17+ -- same substrate-version caveat the RETIRED chash_alias grant carried (MANAGED/cloud is Crunchy Bridge-provided, verified 17.10 as of 2026-07-20; LOCAL always installs our own signed 17.5+ bundle but keeps whatever data directory a pre-bundle install left behind, which can be older). Where MAINTAIN is unavailable this degrades to the SAME graceful path TenantScope#vacuumAnalyze already handles for any permission gap -- the vacuum executor's completion log names the PostgreSQL warning per table, never a crash and never a silent false-positive.

changeSet.author: nexus-hzhgl
changeSet.comment:
nexus-hzhgl (RDR-191 Phase 3/4 pre-flight, conexus relay [22411] ASK B): grant the built-in pg_monitor role to nexus_svc so the engine can read pg_ls_waldir() and the pg_stat_* monitoring views/functions -- WAL-retention visibility during the Phase 4 always-copy trough window (trough = 11,360 MiB - X; breaches the 10,000 MiB floor if retained WAL X exceeds ~1,360 MiB). Before this grant pg_ls_waldir() is permission-denied to nexus_svc, so retained WAL was entirely unobservable.
CAVEAT (conexus relay [22411], correcting an earlier assumption): pg_monitor does NOT provide filesystem free space. It is WAL-retention visibility ONLY -- the disk-free-space gate is a separate ask, conexus's own Crunchy Bridge API key path. Neither substitutes for the other.
WHY THIS SUCCEEDS UNDER A NOSUPERUSER MIGRATION ROLE: granting membership in a role requires the grantor to already hold that role WITH ADMIN OPTION (or be superuser) -- nexus_admin (NOCREATEROLE, NOSUPERUSER) cannot self-provision that the way it can an ordinary schema-owned GRANT. The bootstrap superuser must first run `GRANT pg_monitor TO nexus_admin WITH ADMIN OPTION`, exactly the same shape as nexus_diag's BYPASSRLS in grants-nexus-diag.xml -- an attribute/ privilege only a superuser can confer, so it lives OUTSIDE this changelog: src/nexus/db/pg_provision.py for the local bundle (_create_roles for a from-scratch provision, _backfill_pg_monitor_admin_option from provision()'s fast idempotency path for an EXISTING install -- round 2, code-review-expert Critical 2026-08-13: _create_roles alone is unreached on every already- provisioned local install, the steady state for upgrades), and docs/configuration.md's bring-your-own-Postgres DBA prerequisites for managed deployments.
TRADEOFF, recorded deliberately (substantive-critic round 2, T2 [22418]): WITH ADMIN OPTION lets nexus_admin grant or revoke pg_monitor membership to ANY role, not just nexus_svc -- a small widening of nexus_admin's role-grant blast radius. Accepted because the changelog (running as nexus_admin) is exactly where such grants are supposed to originate as the durable record; the narrower alternative (superuser grants pg_monitor to nexus_svc directly) would bypass the changelog and drift on any credential-domain rebuild.
FAIL-LOUD WITH A NAMED REMEDY, NEVER A SILENT SKIP (round 2, code-review-expert Important 2026-08-13): unlike grants-nexus-diag-1's clean skip-when-absent (an OPTIONAL diagnostic role), nexus_svc's WAL-retention visibility is not optional once shipped, and nothing in code enforces that a bring-your-own/managed deployment's DBA has run the ADMIN OPTION prerequisite before this changeset executes -- especially on the FIRST boot after upgrading to an engine that carries this changeset. Rather than let that surface as a bare "permission denied to grant role pg_monitor" (which names no remedy), the inner GRANT is wrapped to catch exactly that failure and re-raise a self-explanatory error naming the fix -- the same "loud, not silent" posture as grants-nexus-svc-1's REQUIRED-nexus_svc fail-fast, applied to a permission gap instead of a missing role. No MARK_RAN degrade, no preConditions skip: a reproducible, WAL-visibility-is-a-probe absence must never masquerade as a vacuous pass.
IDEMPOTENCY: GRANT of role membership is naturally idempotent in PostgreSQL (re-granting an already-held membership is a no-op); runAlways="true" self-heals a nexus_svc created after the first migration run, same as every other changeset in this file.
pg_monitor is a built-in PostgreSQL role (PG10+) -- no version guard needed, unlike the PG17+-only MAINTAIN privilege above.
